text:
ashley: FYI CI perf alert - runtime/p99 spiked ~3x after the runtime merge that landed ~08:15 UTC (sha 8f3a2d7). Canary rollout auto-paused. dashboard: https://graf.redwood/p/runtimes/p99 :eyes:

mike: saw the alert. which tests are failing? link to CI failure?

perf-bot: [CI job] runtime-e2e-perf #452 failed - p99 latency 3120ms (baseline 980ms). artifacts: https://ci.redwood/jobs/452/artifacts

dina: repro'ed locally on my laptop with gpu-small image. simple load: 
```
./tools/perf_run --model=gpt-small --concurrency=16 --batch=8 --seq=1024 --iters=200
```
p99 jumped from ~1s -> ~3s. I dumped a perf proto and did a quick pprof. Top caller is select_kernel() in kernel_selector.cpp and also a lot of memcpy hotspots from kv_cache.cpp:evict_prefix

ashley: interesting - PR #4219 changed batch/latency heuristics and also touched KV cache eviction timing (small tweak to warmup path). @mike can you kick off a git bisect on the runtime repo?

mike: starting git bisect. bad=8f3a2d7 (HEAD), good=3b1a9f4 (yesterday stable). will run the perf harness on each step but need to parallelize.

sanjay: I can run the harness on our CI runner (g4-small) to speed up. mike, drop the bisect script I'll wrap it.

mike: bisect script: 
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
git bisect start $BAD $GOOD
while git bisect run ./tools/bisect_perf.sh; do :; done
```

./tools/bisect_perf.sh runs the same perf_run with 200 iters and returns nonzero if p99 > 2x baseline.

dina: quick note - local repro is sensitive to kv cache warmup. If you run the run_load with --kv-warmup=0 the regression is less pronounced. That implies the interaction of batching heuristics + warmup could be amplifying the memcpy churn.

mike: first bisect pass landed a suspect: commit 4c7b2a9 changed batch selection thresholds. Running deeper.

ashley: can someone grab a flamegraph from the failing bisect commit and from the good commit and post side-by-side?

sanjay: uploaded two flame svgs: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/ff/good.svg and https://ci.redwood/artifacts/ff/bad.svg

eva: quick eyeball: bad.svg shows heavy time in kernel_selector::score_candidate() and kv_cache::evict_prefix(), good.svg has those flat. Looks like the new batching tries larger batches earlier, causing larger KV cache churn and memcpy.

mike: bisect finished: culprit = commit 5b9d1f2 (part of PR #4219) - change in BatchingHeuristics::should_grow_batch() plus a reordering in kv_cache evict logic.

ashley: nice find. Can we produce a small reproducible test reproducing the p99 delta in CI so we can attach to the PR? We need a deterministic harness that isolates the batching+kv interaction.

dina: created reproducer: tools/repro_kv_batch.py (single-threaded harness that simulates prefix-heavy traffic). Steps: 
1) checkout 3b1a9f4 (good) run ./tools/repro_kv_batch.py --iters=100 -> mean latency 950ms p99 1.02s
2) checkout 5b9d1f2 (bad) run same -> mean 2.8s p99 3.1s
Attach logs and perf proto to PR.

ashley: assign a rollback candidate? might be risky to revert entire PR because it had unrelated batching fixes. Maybe create a targeted revert that only touches the kv_cache evict reorder. Thoughts?

mike: I can craft a narrow revert that preserves batching heuristic changes but restores old evict order. Will run CI perf on that branch.

perf-bot: [Perf run] branch kv-evict-rollout #3 completed: p99 1.05s (baseline 0.98s) -> passes perf gate.

ashley: awesome. Can you open a PR with the rollback and request an expedited review? Tagging @dina @sanjay for quick look.

mike: PR opened: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/4302 - title: "revert(kv): restore evict_prefix ordering to avoid memcopy churn". Added bisect artifacts + reproducer + perf graphs.

dina: ran evict profiling with counters enabled: kv_evictions_per_second jumped ~4x on bad commit because larger batches caused more partial prefix evictions. Logged counters to /tmp/kv_counters.log and attached.

sanjay: safety check: the original reorder was supposed to reduce lock contention for batches > 16. We should add a conditional path: if batch_size > X keep reorder, else old order. I'll draft a patch after the rollback is merged.

ashley: plan: 1) merge revert PR to unpause canary, 2) monitor p99 for 30m, 3) then ship a follow-up with conditional ordering and extra unit coverage.

mike: merging revert now.

perf-bot: [deploy] canary rollout paused -> resumed at 08:53 UTC. Canary p99 back to 1.1s. :thumbsup:

eva: add an integration test that simulates kv-warmup + bursty batch growth so we catch this in future CI perf gates. I'll own that.

ashley: thanks everyone. Great bisect coordination. ACTIONS: mike -> follow-up patch with conditional evict ordering. eva -> integration test. sanjay -> perf regression guard in the canary job to detect prefix-mem spikes. dina -> update PR #4219 with notes on kv-warmup risk.

mike: leaving this thread to doc the bisect steps in the PR and close the loop.

ashley: closing the loop here — please add any stray logs to the PR. Good job! :trophy:
